PullRequest.Title: Agent host: show skill argument-hint as inline placeholder
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #339445

In agent-host chat sessions, a skill's `argument-hint` frontmatter wasn't shown as inline placeholder text after `/skill `, while runtime commands like `/review` and local chat prompts/skills already show theirs. The hint was dropped at every layer of the agent-host skill path. Restoring it makes skills consistent with commands.

## Changes

- **Skill metadata:**
  - `parseSkillFile` now reads `argument-hint` (trimmed; a blank value is ignored).
  - Plugin and Claude skills carry the hint through `readSkills` and `toParsedSkill`.
  - Copilot discovery prefers the SDK-reported `ServerSkill.argumentHint` and falls back to the frontmatter.
  - The hint lives in a namespaced `_meta` key, `vscode.skill.argumentHint`, on `SkillCustomization`, with a typed reader and writer in `common/meta`. The synced protocol types are unchanged. Hosts that don't publish the key behave exactly as before.
- **Completions:** skill completion `_meta` gains an optional `argumentHint`, alongside the existing command `argumentHint`.
- **Rendering:** the Agents window placeholder and the workbench `InputEditorCommandArgumentHint` now accept agent-host skill references as well as commands. They still show the hint only while the command or skill is the sole input followed by one space.

## Testing

1. Create `~/.copilot/skills/design-prep/SKILL.md` with `argument-hint: "<problem and repo> [offline]"` and `user-invocable: true`.
2. In an Agents window Copilot CLI session, type `/design-prep ` and accept the completion. The hint appears as grey placeholder text.
3. Type any character. The hint disappears.
4. Check that `/review ` still shows its hint.
5. Check that a skill without `argument-hint` shows no placeholder.
6. Check that a skill installed from a plugin with an `argument-hint` shows its hint.

Unit tests cover the parser, the `_meta` reader and writer, Copilot discovery (SDK hint and frontmatter fallback), the completion provider, and both renderers. Lint and the layers check are clean for the changed files.

Caveats:
- I verified this with unit tests only, not in a running Agents window.
- Codex skills and legacy `commands/*.md` files are out of scope.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The added guard, per-model-change subscription, exact call path, and allocating text-buffer API are all explicit in repository code. Only the user-visible magnitude varies with prompt size and edit count.
Findings.PerformanceResource: CPU spent traversing the text model and bytes allocated for the full suffix string
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For one accepted hinted skill followed by P characters, E subsequent model edits copy up to P characters each, for O(E*P) work and allocation; when the prompt is built incrementally this can become quadratic in its final length.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased synchronous input latency, allocation/GC pressure, and possible dropped frames
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The command-only guard skipped every skill reference, so editing a prompt accepted from a skill completion did not perform this suffix extraction.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The broadened guard now lets Skill references with argumentHint metadata reach isCommandOnlyContent during every input-model update; that method materializes the entire text after the skill reference with model.getValueInRange before comparing it with a one-character string.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 92 changes the filter from `!== AgentHostCompletionReferenceKind.Command` to `=== undefined`, newly allowing Skill references into the hint-rendering path.
Findings.Title: Reject non-empty skill arguments before copying the prompt
Findings.Impact: Editing a long prompt after a hinted `/skill` completion adds synchronous O(prompt length) traversal/allocation to each keystroke, causing input latency and GC pressure and potentially dropped frames for large pasted logs or code.
Findings.Evidence: The constructor subscribes update() directly to inputEditor.onDidChangeModelContent; the changed line admits skills, getArgumentHintDecoration calls isCommandOnlyContent, and line 130 reads the range from the skill through the full model end. The piece-tree implementation returns a string for getValueInRange, so a prompt such as `/design-prep <large pasted log or code>` is copied again on every subsequent edit even though any suffix longer than one character already proves the hint must be hidden.
Findings.Recommendation: Use range/model positions or a length check to reject suffixes whose length is not exactly one before reading text, and read only that single character when it can still be the required space.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The per-edit subscription, existing first range lookup, newly reachable second lookup, and suffix allocation are explicit. The exact frame impact depends on prompt length, but the duplicated scaling work is certain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: CPU for duplicate full-string searches and bytes allocated by the suffix slice
Findings.PerformanceScaling: With one accepted hinted skill, each of E edits over a P-character prompt adds another O(P) reference search and up to O(P) suffix allocation; additional attachments are also rescanned until the skill entry is reached.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Higher synchronous rendering/input latency with additional allocation and GC pressure
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Skill entries were rejected by the command-only guard. The decoration updater located each inserted skill reference once for its normal inline decoration, but did not perform the second hint-specific full-text lookup or suffix slice.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The broadened attachment guard now runs hinted Skill entries through getAgentHostCompletionAttachmentRange and suffix slicing whenever the Sessions input decorations update.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 144 replaces the command-only check with an undefined-kind check, newly sending Skill attachments through the full hint lookup on every decoration update.
Findings.Title: Reuse the resolved skill range when updating the hint
Findings.Impact: Editing a long Agents/Sessions prompt that starts with a hinted `/skill` repeats full-text scanning and suffix allocation on the synchronous input path, increasing typing latency and GC pressure and risking dropped frames for prompts containing large pasted logs or code.
Findings.Evidence: _registerDecorations invokes _updateDecorations on every editor model change. _updateDecorations first calls getAgentHostCompletionAttachmentRange for every inserted reference, then calls _getArgumentHintDecorations; after the changed guard admits a hinted skill, getCommandArgumentHintPlaceholder calls the same range finder again and evaluates value.slice(range.endExclusive). getAgentHostCompletionAttachmentRange searches the complete value for all occurrences to choose the closest match, so the hint path duplicates a full-prompt search and allocates the remaining suffix per edit.
Findings.Recommendation: Carry the range already resolved in _updateDecorations into the hint calculation (or use the tracked range directly), then compare offsets/length and charAt without searching the full value again or slicing its suffix.

Scenarios.Scenario: Discover Copilot, plugin, and Claude skills and publish argument-hint metadata
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Copilot discovery waits for the existing SDK skills.discover RPC and then the existing parseSkillFile reads before publishing customizations. Plugin/Claude discovery likewise waits for existing directory resolution and one SKILL.md read per effective skill. The diff only extracts and carries one more already-parsed frontmatter string.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One skills.discover call per existing discovery request, independent of skill count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same SDK discovery RPC was already awaited.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The RPC must finish before skill customizations can be published.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One read per effective skill file; grouping/deduplication and Promise.all behavior are unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: parseSkillFile already read every same file to obtain name, description, and invocation flags; the diff only reads argument-hint from the existing parse result.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Reads complete before the corresponding discovery result is assembled.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number S of discovered non-builtin, non-plugin SDK skills for the Copilot path, or effective skill files after directory enumeration and name deduplication for plugin paths.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Copilot skill files are parsed with the pre-existing Promise.all over discovered skills. Plugin directories and children are also processed with pre-existing Promise.all fan-out; the diff adds no limiter and does not increase operation cardinality.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new cache or cache key is introduced. Cold filesystem reads and warm OS/file-service cache behavior are unchanged; successful, blank, and missing argument hints all reuse the same parsed file result.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed hunks consume values from existing parser/RPC results and add no boundary call.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Skill counts and filesystem latency vary, but boundary cardinality is provably unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable discovery regression; added string trimming and metadata storage scale with existing skill count and are small relative to unchanged I/O.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each slash-triggered completion awaits the existing agent.getChatCustomizations call, scans effective customizations, filters/deduplicates candidates, and serializes completion attachment metadata. The diff adds one metadata read/trim and an optional short string field per skill candidate.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Retrieve the agent's effective chat customizations
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing retrieval per slash completion request, not per skill.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The provider already made the same retrieval and full candidate scan on each matching completion request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Completion candidates cannot be produced until retrieval resolves.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Build completion attachment metadata for matching skills
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One attachment object per deduplicated matching skill; the diff adds at most one optional hint string reference.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same attachment was built without argumentHint.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous on the completion response path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of effective user-invocable skills after enablement filtering and name/description deduplication.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One completion request at a time from the editor provider with cancellation checks; candidate processing is synchronous and serial after customization retrieval.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Host customization snapshots and agent-specific customization behavior are unchanged. The optional hint is read from the already-published snapshot; no positive/negative cache or miss behavior changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the provider and metadata helper code directly establish the path and cardinality.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Installed skill count varies, but the added per-candidate field and trim are bounded by existing metadata and do not change asymptotic behavior.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable completion-generation regression; no new boundary or extra candidate pass is introduced.

Scenarios.Scenario: Edit a workbench chat prompt after accepting a hinted skill completion
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Every input model change synchronously calls update, scans dynamic variables, and now admits the skill reference into isCommandOnlyContent before repainting decorations.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Prompt suffix length P and number E of edits after one hinted skill reference; effective reference cardinality is normally one leading skill, with any other dynamic references scanned serially.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Fully serialized on the UI/editor model-change event; no batching, deferral, cancellation, or backpressure.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cached eligibility state or coalescing exists; the suffix check is recomputed for every model change even after argument text guarantees the hint is hidden.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed guard, event subscription, full-range getValueInRange call, and string-producing piece-tree implementation were traced directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact frame impact depends on prompt length and edit cadence, but large pasted code/log prompts followed by edits are realistic.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable synchronous UI regression: newly enabled skill hints copy up to the full prompt suffix on every edit.

Scenarios.Scenario: Edit a Sessions/Agents-window prompt after accepting a hinted skill completion
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Every model change synchronously rebuilds decorations, resolves each inserted reference, then now admits the hinted skill into a second range lookup and suffix check before setting the hint decoration.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Prompt length P, edit count E, and attachment/reference count R; one hinted leading skill is enough to add the duplicate full-text search.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Fully serialized in the editor model-change callback; no coalescing or deferred rendering.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The already-resolved reference range from the normal decoration pass is not reused by the hint pass. No result is cached across edits.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed guard, per-change callback, first existing range lookup, second newly reachable lookup, and suffix slice are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Prompt sizes vary, but large logs/code are a normal chat input and the duplicate scan/allocation occurs deterministically for each subsequent edit.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable repeated synchronous work: hinted skills add another O(P) search and suffix allocation per edit on top of the existing decoration lookup.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all 14 changed files and all diff pages for the performance focus. Discovery and completion metadata propagation preserve existing I/O cardinality and concurrency. Two concrete synchronous editing regressions were reported, one in each hint-rendering surface.
